text_boxes.text: Temporal stability, numerical repair and the value of transaction history

Clipping repairs severe LR degradation; more history does not deliver stable gains.
At the same review capacity, the dates receiving extreme scores can change the conclusion.
Under the same limited review capacity, do numerical repair and richer history improve fraud ranking across time? We separate preprocessing effects, feature increments and date composition.

IEEE-CIS / Vesta [1]: 590,540 labeled transactions, 20,663 fraud labels, 394 raw columns and 182 relative day buckets. Identity is audit-only. ID, target and split time are excluded from model inputs.
Evaluate days [61,89) and [89,117). Overlapping expanding training windows are not independent replications. Validation/test share one 413,378-row fitted snapshot.
7 candidates x 3 snapshots = 21 core fits, plus 3 legacy reruns. All 9 LR fits converged. Parameters and candidates are fixed; no large search or test-based winner selection.
Same history; missing entities keep history missing.
+4 fields: card1/addr1 24h counts and elapsed time.
LR: balanced classes, L-BFGS, max_iter=1000; rank by decision_function. LightGBM: 300 trees, learning rate 0.05, 31 leaves, min_child_samples=20; balanced classes, seed 42.
TRAIN ONLY Fit clipping, imputation, encoding and scaling on training data. Clip amount, dist1/2 and C/D/V numeric fields.
STRICT PAST History uses card1 and addr1 inputs at times <t, never labels; 24h windows are [t-86400,t).
TIED TIMES Compute all rows at one timestamp before updating state. Normalize codes such as 123 and 123.0 consistently.
Training labels are assumed available at each cutoff; actual arrival times are unknown. Previously viewed test results remain retrospective. Anonymous entity codes are not verified identities.

K = ceil(r x N); hits = fraud labels in the top K.
Precision = hits/K; recall = hits/total fraud.
Primary r=0.5%; also 0.1%, 1%, 2% and legacy Top100/500. AP is average precision [3].

Main contrasts: LR2-LR0 and H3-H0. Each period uses 1,000 paired 3-day moving-block draws for percentile 95% intervals. Daily 8/16/32-review scenarios match the global comparator's actual total capacity.
Fraud hits at 0.5% period capacity. Column budgets differ with evaluation size; compare models within each period. Test contains 3,083 fraud labels.
Amount ranking: 8/443; random conditional expectation: 15.42/443. LR0 probability ranking gives 6 hits; margin ranking gives 0. Removing probability saturation alone does not repair the ranking.
Y: precision (%). X: review rate. H0/H3 are close; LR0 fails most severely at tight capacity. Complete seven-model results remain in the evidence.
H3-H0 changes sign: +2, -11, +4, -7. Every main 3-day interval crosses zero; this does not establish equivalence. AP and top-K hits describe different ranking regions.
Clipping drives the repair. LR1-LR0: +27/+13/+13/+376 hits. Stronger L2 (LR2-LR1): -3/-1/-4/+7 across F1/F2/validation/test; no consistent extra gain.
394 columns x 3 partitions: missingness, unique values, constants, quantiles, non-finite/unseen values and train-range exceedances. Raw maxima:
V323 median: 733 on days 171-172, 0 on other test days (nonmissing). Score contributions and date concentration support an extreme-input diagnosis, not a unique causal explanation.
LR0 top 443 reviews: 442 from two dates; 0 hits.
One review remains on day 181. Duplicate inputs are also audited; identical anonymous fields alone do not prove leakage. No automatic deduplication.
Test: 16 reviews/day = 496 slots. Compare with the same 496 global reviews; differences are daily minus global hits.
LR0: +301 hits, 3-day 95% interval [-38, 341.02]. LR2/H0/H3 lose 53/26/24 hits. This end-of-day batch scenario gives no universal improvement.

Omit days 171-172: LR0 daily advantage flips
+301 to -8 hits; LR2 still leads LR0 by
87 hits (362 vs 275; 414 period slots).
Fixed models, scores and history; evaluation rows are filtered and budgets rematched. All 332 continuous 1/2/7-day omission windows are reported; the full test remains primary.
Test H3-H0 = -7 hits. Post-hoc block-length checks retain the original 3-day result:
7-day blocks give a negative interval; 1/3-day blocks cross zero. None supports stable positive history gains. LR2-LR0 is positive on test at all three block lengths, with weaker evidence elsewhere.
Fixed-model intervals omit training uncertainty and multiplicity correction. 31 test day buckets limit small-effect and long-term claims; resampling adds no new months.
10 correctness tests passed. Independent checks: 36 period/config groups, 4,320 daily groups and 76,995 queue records.
Supplement: 1,182 missingness values, 28 baseline metric groups and 259 independent omission/model checks.
Clean environment: install, pip check, 10 tests and synthetic pipeline passed; no real-data refit.
Train-only clipping restores much of the LR ranking.
History gains do not persist across evaluation periods.
Next: a genuinely unseen labeled period under a fixed protocol.
Scope: retrospective ranking, uncalibrated scores and assumed review budgets. No verified deployment, causal mechanism, label-delay model, financial return or long-run staffing optimum is claimed.

Sources: verified study_20261121_01; executed_summary.json; supplement_20261121_01; frozen plan2. [1] Kaggle / Vesta, IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection (2019). [2] Ke et al., LightGBM, NeurIPS (2017). [3] Saito & Rehmsmeier, precision-recall evaluation, PLOS ONE (2015).
